transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because for a long time now, my sleep has just been broken. I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm usually up before my alarm even goes off, feeling like I never really rested at all.
Aside from your sleep troubles, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or sad?

Yes, I suppose I have. It's... well, most days I just feel like the color has gone out of things. Even when I'm doing something nice, like sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, or looking at art I used to really enjoy. It's all just kind of flat. And I find that I have to work really hard not to just tear up for no clear reason.
About how long have you been feeling this down and flat?

Well, it's been quite a while. I'd say this has been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us, which was... yeah, a little over two years ago now. It's just been pretty much like this ever since.
During these past two years, has there ever been a stretch of time, say two months or more, where you felt completely back to your usual self?
No, I don't think so. There might be a day or two here and there where things feel a little lighter, but... no, never a whole two months. It's just been a constant low for the whole two years.
Before this past two-year period began, had you ever experienced a time in your life when you felt depressed or down like this?
No, not like this. I mean, everyone gets sad sometimes, but before she moved in, I always bounced back. I never felt this... stuck, I guess, for such a long time.
Over this time, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight?

Yes, I have. I really just don't have much of an appetite anymore. I mostly just end up picking at whatever I make for everyone else, or maybe I'll just grab a piece of toast after my shift. Because of that, my clothes have been hanging a lot looser lately, without me even trying to lose weight.
Have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness, or feeling excessively guilty about things?
No, I wouldn't say I feel worthless. And I don't feel guilty about anything, really. I just feel down and tired all the time, but I don't blame myself for it or feel like I'm a bad person.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't. I mean, I feel tired and down, but I've never thought about hurting myself. I don't have any thoughts like that.
Have you been feeling hopeless about the future?

No, I wouldn't say hopeless. I mean, I know things will just keep going on. I don't really think the future is completely bleak or anything like that. I'm mostly just focused on getting through my shifts and taking it one day at a time, really.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making everyday decisions?

No, not really. I mean, my job takes a lot of focus, making sure my clients get their meds on time and all that, and I haven't had any slip-ups. I'm just... tired doing it. But my concentration is fine, and I don't have any trouble making decisions.
Have you or anyone else noticed that you are moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the other hand, feeling unusually restless and fidgety?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. Nobody else has said anything to me about it, either. I mean, I move at my normal pace at work and at home. I'm not slowing down or feeling jittery and restless. Just regular, really.
Have you been experiencing a persistent lack of energy or feeling fatigued nearly every day?

Yes, I definitely have. It's pretty much every day. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and get back to help out at my own house, my body just feels heavy. It gets to the point where even just... charting my work notes or folding a basket of laundry can feel like it's just too much to push through. I'm just completely drained by the end of it all.
Over these past two years, has there ever been a time when your symptoms became noticeably more severe?
No, I don't think so. It hasn't really spiked or gotten noticeably worse at any point. It's just... a constant thing, really. Day in and day out, it pretty much stays about the same.
